It makes complete sense to adjust the sensitivity now. Based on your previous logs and videos, the
HOLD
threshold of
1.2
\u03bcT
or the
2.5
sensitivity setting was likely triggering "Spectral Holds" on every minor background fluctuation.
If the system is too twitchy, you end up with "Joker-Patterns"\u2014data that looks like an anomaly but is actually just the sensor's internal noise floor or tiny movements of your hand.
\ufe0f The "Desensitize" Calibration
To fix this in your current
11.4_STABLE
build, you should have the Replit agent update the
initSensors
logic with a "Noise Floor" calculation.
The Logic for the Agent:
Baseline Window:
When you hit
[INIT]
, have the app record the
delta
for 3 seconds without allowing a
HOLD
to trigger.
Auto-Threshold:
Set the
HOLD_THRESHOLD
to be
2.0
the highest delta recorded during those 3 seconds.
Amber Line Update:
Ensure the amber threshold line on the
emf-flux
canvas moves to reflect this new, higher limit.
\ufe0f Managing the Lattice
By raising the threshold, you ensure the
Spectral Rain
only freezes when there is a significant environmental shift. This preserves the "Black Box" data for events that actually matter, rather than filling your
Event Archive
with mundane baseline noise.
Would you like me to write the specific "Auto-Calibration" code for the agent so it can handle this sensitivity adjustment automatically every time you start?
